sentence: The monthly review notes an increase ___ requests for flexible hours.
setupText: Choose the edit that identifies what increased, without supplying a numerical size for the increase.
taskText: The monthly review notes an increase ___ requests for flexible hours.
text: Choose the edit that identifies what increased, without supplying a numerical size for the increase. The monthly review notes an increase ___ requests for flexible hours.
options: to
in
by
from
answer: in
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2581:Entity versus measure after increase
explanation: 'An increase in requests' identifies the thing becoming more numerous.

rationales.to: 'An increase to' normally introduces a new level or target; requests here are what increased.
rationales.by: 'An increase by' introduces the size of a change, not the category changing.
rationales.in: 'An increase in requests' identifies the thing becoming more numerous.
rationales.from: 'An increase from' introduces a starting level or source rather than the thing increasing.

sentence: The complaint relates to the new booking system.
setupText: Choose the summary that preserves the relationship without adding a cause.
taskText: The complaint relates to the new booking system.
text: Choose the summary that preserves the relationship without adding a cause. The complaint relates to the new booking system.
options: The complaint concerns the new booking system.
The complaint caused the new booking system to fail.
The new booking system was introduced because of the complaint.
The complaint confirms that the new booking system is faulty.
answer: The complaint concerns the new booking system.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2582:Relation to without causal entailment
explanation: 'Relates to' identifies a connection or subject; it does not itself explain causation.

rationales.The complaint caused the new booking sys: A relation to the system does not establish that the complaint caused a failure.
rationales.The complaint concerns the new booking s: 'Relates to' identifies a connection or subject; it does not itself explain causation.
rationales.The new booking system was introduced be: This adds a causal history that 'relates to' does not provide.
rationales.The complaint confirms that the new book: A complaint about a system does not by itself confirm a fault.

sentence: The warning symbol is familiar to most staff.
setupText: Choose the edit preserving who recognizes what.
taskText: The warning symbol is familiar to most staff.
text: Choose the edit preserving who recognizes what. The warning symbol is familiar to most staff.
options: The warning symbol makes most staff familiar with the danger.
Most staff have become familiar to the warning's designer.
Most staff are familiar with the warning symbol.
Most staff are familiar with designing warning symbols.
answer: Most staff are familiar with the warning symbol.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2583:Familiar to and with under perspective change
explanation: A thing can be familiar to people; those people are familiar with the thing.

rationales.The warning symbol makes most staff fami: Recognizing the symbol does not establish that it teaches staff about the danger.
rationales.Most staff have become familiar to the w: This makes the staff recognizable to a different person.
rationales.Most staff are familiar with the warning: A thing can be familiar to people; those people are familiar with the thing.
rationales.Most staff are familiar with designing w: This changes recognition of a symbol into knowledge of designing symbols.

sentence: The manager objected to postponing the inspection.
setupText: Choose the edit that says the manager opposed postponement, not that the manager proposed it.
taskText: The manager objected to postponing the inspection.
text: Choose the edit that says the manager opposed postponement, not that the manager proposed it. The manager objected to postponing the inspection.
options: The manager raised a request for postponement.
The manager raised an objection during the postponed inspection.
The manager objected on behalf of those seeking postponement.
The manager raised an objection to the postponement.
answer: The manager raised an objection to the postponement.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2584:Opposed object across verb and noun constructions
explanation: Both 'object to' and 'an objection to' identify what is opposed.

rationales.The manager raised a request for postpon: A request for postponement seeks it; an objection opposes it.
rationales.The manager raised an objection to the p: Both 'object to' and 'an objection to' identify what is opposed.
rationales.The manager raised an objection during t: This changes the opposed action into the time of a different objection.
rationales.The manager objected on behalf of those: This identifies represented people but does not preserve opposition to postponement itself.

sentence: 'Will we approve the application?' 'That depends on whether the missing records arrive.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation supported by this reply, without assuming the records will be complete.
taskText: 'Will we approve the application?' 'That depends on whether the missing records arrive.'
text: Choose the interpretation supported by this reply, without assuming the records will be complete. 'Will we approve the application?' 'That depends on whether the missing records arrive.'
options: The records will arrive once the application is approved.
Approval has already been granted subject to a delivery date.
The application will be approved as soon as any record arrives.
The arrival of the records affects the approval decision.
answer: The arrival of the records affects the approval decision.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2585:Conditional dependence without an automatic outcome
explanation: 'Depends on whether' makes arrival relevant to the decision without settling the outcome.

rationales.The records will arrive once the applica: This reverses the direction of dependence and adds a promised arrival.
rationales.Approval has already been granted subjec: The reply leaves the decision open; it does not announce approval or a date.
rationales.The application will be approved as soon: This turns an unspecified dependence into a definite automatic trigger.
rationales.The arrival of the records affects the a: 'Depends on whether' makes arrival relevant to the decision without settling the outcome.

sentence: The report examines the effect of night shifts on sleep.
setupText: Choose the statement that preserves the direction of influence.
taskText: The report examines the effect of night shifts on sleep.
text: Choose the statement that preserves the direction of influence. The report examines the effect of night shifts on sleep.
options: It examines how night shifts affect sleep.
It examines how sleep affects the allocation of night shifts.
It examines the effect of sleep on working at night.
It examines whether night shifts and sleep have the same causes.
answer: It examines how night shifts affect sleep.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2586:Direction in effect of X on Y
explanation: 'The effect of X on Y' makes X the influence and Y the affected thing.

rationales.It examines how sleep affects the alloca: This reverses the influence and adds a scheduling decision.
rationales.It examines how night shifts affect slee: 'The effect of X on Y' makes X the influence and Y the affected thing.
rationales.It examines the effect of sleep on worki: This makes sleep the influence rather than the outcome being affected.
rationales.It examines whether night shifts and sle: Shared causes are a different relationship from the effect of one on the other.

sentence: Which description assigns leadership?
setupText: Choose the sentence that says Mira accepted responsibility for the project, not merely membership of its team.
taskText: Which description assigns leadership?
text: Choose the sentence that says Mira accepted responsibility for the project, not merely membership of its team. Which description assigns leadership?
options: Mira took part in the project.
Mira took charge of the project.
Mira took an interest in the project.
Mira took advice on the project.
answer: Mira took charge of the project.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2587:Leadership of versus participation in
explanation: 'Take charge of' means assume control or responsibility.

'Take part in' describes participation without assigning leadership.
Interest does not establish that Mira leads or manages the work.
'Take charge of' means assume control or responsibility.
Receiving advice does not assign Mira authority over the project.

sentence: Admission was free of charge for the residents.
setupText: Choose the rewrite that preserves the residents' exemption from an admission charge.
taskText: Admission was free of charge for the residents.
text: Choose the rewrite that preserves the residents' exemption from an admission charge. Admission was free of charge for the residents.
options: The residents did not have to pay to enter.
The residents were free to set the admission charge.
The residents were paid for entering the building.
The residents could charge other visitors for admission.
answer: The residents did not have to pay to enter.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2588:Exemption expressed by free of charge
explanation: 'Free of charge' means no payment is required; 'for the residents' limits who receives that benefit.

rationales.The residents were free to set the admis: This turns exemption from payment into authority to choose a price.
rationales.The residents did not have to pay to ent: 'Free of charge' means no payment is required; 'for the residents' limits who receives that benefit.
rationales.The residents were paid for entering the: No charge is not the same as receiving payment.
rationales.The residents could charge other visitor: The sentence grants residents no permission to collect fees.

sentence: The office promises a reply no later than two working days after receiving your message.
setupText: Choose the sentence that gives a maximum waiting time, allowing an earlier reply.
taskText: The office promises a reply no later than two working days after receiving your message.
text: Choose the sentence that gives a maximum waiting time, allowing an earlier reply. The office promises a reply no later than two working days after receiving your message.
options: We will reply after two working days of receiving your message.
We will reply for two working days after receiving your message.
We will reply in exactly two working days after receiving your message.
We will reply within two working days of receiving your message.
answer: We will reply within two working days of receiving your message.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2589:Maximum elapsed time with within
explanation: 'Within' gives an outer time limit measured from the specified starting event.

rationales.We will reply after two working days of: 'After' places the reply beyond the stated waiting period rather than within it.
rationales.We will reply for two working days after: 'For' makes two days the duration of replying, not a response deadline.
rationales.We will reply in exactly two working day: 'Exactly' rules out an earlier reply that the promise permits.
rationales.We will reply within two working days of: 'Within' gives an outer time limit measured from the specified starting event.

sentence: The lock was opened with a special key by a technician.
setupText: The technician performed the action, and the key was the tool. Choose the active sentence preserving those roles.
taskText: The lock was opened with a special key by a technician.
text: The technician performed the action, and the key was the tool. Choose the active sentence preserving those roles. The lock was opened with a special key by a technician.
options: A technician made a special key after the lock was opened.
A technician used a special key to open the lock.
A special key was made by the technician who opened the lock.
A technician opened the lock for the owner of a special key.
answer: A technician used a special key to open the lock.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2590:Passive agent by versus instrument with
explanation: In this passive sentence, 'by' names the agent and 'with' names the instrument.

rationales.A technician made a special key after th: This adds key-making and changes the order; the key was the opening instrument.
rationales.A technician used a special key to open: In this passive sentence, 'by' names the agent and 'with' names the instrument.
rationales.A special key was made by the technician: The original says nothing about who made the key.
rationales.A technician opened the lock for the own: This changes the key's role from instrument to something owned by an added beneficiary.

sentence: Which description names the room's intended use?
setupText: Choose the version stating that study is the purpose of the room, not that study is currently taking place.
taskText: Which description names the room's intended use?
text: Choose the version stating that study is the purpose of the room, not that study is currently taking place. Which description names the room's intended use?
options: This room is for quiet study.
Quiet study is taking place in this room.
This room is beside the quiet study area.
This room was occupied during quiet study.
answer: This room is for quiet study.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2591:Intended use for versus actual activity in
explanation: 'For' introduces intended use; the room need not be occupied at this moment.

rationales.Quiet study is taking place in this room: This describes current activity, not the room's designated purpose.
rationales.This room is beside the quiet study area: This locates the room near a study area rather than assigning its use.
'For' introduces intended use; the room need not be occupied at this moment.
rationales.This room was occupied during quiet stud: This reports a past occasion, not the room's purpose.

sentence: The partners cannot agree how to divide the costs.
setupText: Choose the wording that reports a disagreement about money, without claiming the people dislike each other.
taskText: The partners cannot agree how to divide the costs.
text: Choose the wording that reports a disagreement about money, without claiming the people dislike each other. The partners cannot agree how to divide the costs.
options: They are hostile towards each other.
They compete for control of the partnership.
They have withdrawn from the partnership.
They disagree over the division of costs.
answer: They disagree over the division of costs.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2592:Issue in dispute introduced by over
explanation: 'Over' introduces the issue in dispute; it does not itself describe personal animosity.

This adds personal hostility beyond disagreement over one issue.
rationales.They disagree over the division of costs: 'Over' introduces the issue in dispute; it does not itself describe personal animosity.
rationales.They compete for control of the partners: This changes a cost dispute into a struggle for control.
rationales.They have withdrawn from the partnership: The disagreement does not establish that either person has left.

sentence: The flat is ready to rent ___ a faulty kitchen light.
setupText: Choose the completion meaning that one remaining problem is excluded from a generally positive assessment.
taskText: The flat is ready to rent ___ a faulty kitchen light.
text: Choose the completion meaning that one remaining problem is excluded from a generally positive assessment. The flat is ready to rent ___ a faulty kitchen light.
options: because of
in addition to
in exchange for
apart from
answer: apart from
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2593:Exception to an assessment with apart from
explanation: Here 'apart from' marks an exception: the light remains a problem despite general readiness.

rationales.because of: This makes the faulty light a reason the flat is ready, not an exception to readiness.
rationales.in addition to: This adds the faulty light without expressing the intended exception to the assessment.
rationales.apart from: Here 'apart from' marks an exception: the light remains a problem despite general readiness.
rationales.in exchange for: This describes a trade, not a qualification to the flat's condition.

sentence: The outdoor market stayed open ___ the heavy rain.
setupText: Choose the phrase that presents the rain as an obstacle the event continued through, not the reason for continuing.
taskText: The outdoor market stayed open ___ the heavy rain.
text: Choose the phrase that presents the rain as an obstacle the event continued through, not the reason for continuing. The outdoor market stayed open ___ the heavy rain.
options: despite
because of
in preparation for
in the absence of
answer: despite
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2594:Concession with despite a noun phrase
explanation: 'Despite' marks a contrast between the difficult weather and the market staying open.

rationales.because of: This presents the rain as the cause of staying open.
rationales.despite: 'Despite' marks a contrast between the difficult weather and the market staying open.
rationales.in preparation for: This makes staying open preparation for rain, rather than continuation through an obstacle.
rationales.in the absence of: This says the rain was not present, contrary to the stated situation.

sentence: The drawing is ___ the designer.
setupText: Choose the phrase that means the drawing is useful to the designer, without identifying who made it.
taskText: The drawing is ___ the designer.
text: Choose the phrase that means the drawing is useful to the designer, without identifying who made it. The drawing is ___ the designer.
options: the work of
under review by
of use to
on loan from
answer: of use to
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2595:Beneficial relation in of use to
explanation: 'Of use to someone' means useful to that person and does not assign authorship.

rationales.the work of: This attributes authorship to the designer instead of describing usefulness.
rationales.under review by: This says the designer is examining it, not that it is useful.
rationales.of use to: 'Of use to someone' means useful to that person and does not assign authorship.
rationales.on loan from: This makes the designer the source of a loan, not necessarily the beneficiary.

sentence: The volunteers continued answering calls until eight.
setupText: Choose the edit that preserves duration, not a deadline for finishing.
taskText: The volunteers continued answering calls until eight.
text: Choose the edit that preserves duration, not a deadline for finishing. The volunteers continued answering calls until eight.
options: The volunteers had answered the calls by eight.
The volunteers kept answering calls up to eight.
The volunteers began answering calls at eight.
The volunteers agreed before eight to answer calls.
answer: The volunteers kept answering calls up to eight.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2596:Activity endpoint versus completed result
explanation: 'Until' and 'up to' here give the endpoint of a continuing activity.

rationales.The volunteers had answered the calls by: 'By eight' reports completion no later than eight, not continued activity up to that time.
rationales.The volunteers kept answering calls up t: 'Until' and 'up to' here give the endpoint of a continuing activity.
rationales.The volunteers began answering calls at: This changes the endpoint into a starting time.
rationales.The volunteers agreed before eight to an: This places an agreement earlier than eight and no longer reports the actual answering period.

sentence: According to the building manager, the lift will reopen tomorrow.
setupText: Choose the sentence that accurately reports the named source without claiming independent confirmation.
taskText: According to the building manager, the lift will reopen tomorrow.
text: Choose the sentence that accurately reports the named source without claiming independent confirmation. According to the building manager, the lift will reopen tomorrow.
options: The lift's reopening tomorrow has been independently confirmed.
The building manager says the lift will reopen tomorrow.
The building manager has been told to reopen the lift tomorrow.
The lift will reopen tomorrow in agreement with the building manager.
answer: The building manager says the lift will reopen tomorrow.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2597:Information attribution with according to
explanation: 'According to' names the source of the information while leaving its independent accuracy open.

rationales.The lift's reopening tomorrow has been i: 'According to' attributes a claim; it does not report independent verification.
rationales.The building manager says the lift will: 'According to' names the source of the information while leaving its independent accuracy open.
rationales.The building manager has been told to re: This turns a sourced prediction into an instruction to the manager.
rationales.The lift will reopen tomorrow in agreeme: Agreement or consent is a different relationship from being the source of a report.

sentence: The airline attributed the delay ___ a staffing problem.
setupText: Choose the phrase that identifies the explanation offered for the delay, not its duration.
taskText: The airline attributed the delay ___ a staffing problem.
text: Choose the phrase that identifies the explanation offered for the delay, not its duration. The airline attributed the delay ___ a staffing problem.
options: for
with
to
from
answer: to
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2598:Proposed cause after attribute to
explanation: 'Attribute X to Y' identifies Y as the explanation offered for X.

rationales.for: 'For' can introduce a duration after delay, but 'attribute something for a cause' is not this verb's pattern.
rationales.with: 'With' can express accompaniment; attribution takes 'to' before the proposed cause.
rationales.to: 'Attribute X to Y' identifies Y as the explanation offered for X.
rationales.from: Although 'a delay resulting from a problem' is possible, the verb attribute requires 'to' in this construction.

sentence: I am relying on Kim to check the figures before publication.
setupText: Choose the concise rewrite that preserves both the person and the thing the speaker is relying on.
taskText: I am relying on Kim to check the figures before publication.
text: Choose the concise rewrite that preserves both the person and the thing the speaker is relying on. I am relying on Kim to check the figures before publication.
options: I am checking the figures for Kim before publication.
I am checking with Kim whether the figures have been published.
I am counting on Kim to check the figures before publication.
I am accounting for Kim's figures before publication.
answer: I am counting on Kim to check the figures before publication.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2599:Reliance on a person to act
explanation: 'Count on someone to do something' expresses reliance on that person's action.

rationales.I am checking the figures for Kim before: This makes the speaker the checker and Kim the beneficiary.
rationales.I am counting on Kim to check the figure: 'Count on someone to do something' expresses reliance on that person's action.
rationales.I am checking with Kim whether the figur: This asks Kim for information about publication rather than relying on Kim's checking.
rationales.I am accounting for Kim's figures before: 'Account for' means explain or justify here; it does not express reliance on Kim.

sentence: The proposal is under consideration.
setupText: Choose the wording that means the subject is being examined now, without saying a decision has been made.
taskText: The proposal is under consideration.
text: Choose the wording that means the subject is being examined now, without saying a decision has been made. The proposal is under consideration.
options: The proposal has been accepted with conditions.
The proposal has been removed from consideration.
The proposal is being considered.
The proposal will be submitted for consideration.
answer: The proposal is being considered.
focusKey: coverage-prepositions-b2-2600:Current process expressed by under consideration
explanation: 'Under consideration' describes a current process, not its eventual outcome.

rationales.The proposal has been accepted with cond: Conditional acceptance is a decision; consideration alone does not establish acceptance.
rationales.The proposal has been removed from consi: 'Removed from' means it is no longer being considered, reversing the statement.
rationales.The proposal will be submitted for consi: This places submission in the future rather than saying examination is happening now.
'Under consideration' describes a current process, not its eventual outcome.
